# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 68 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 68 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_068_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 6, Part 6 — Various Kinds of Sinners

**68:1** "I wish also to know, lord," I said, "why the Lord does not keep away from his servants the troubles and adversities of this life, but instead delivers them to these things." "He cannot," he said, "keep them away, for they must pass through all these things. The Lord has appointed these torments for the testing of those whom he has appointed to such a test."

**68:2** "But why, lord, are some tested with few torments and others with many?" "Because," he said, "not all can endure equally. For some are weak in faith and some are strong. The strong must endure the greater trials, that they may be perfected; but the weak receive fewer trials, that they may not be completely broken."

**68:3** "Now the Lord watches over all the afflicted and will give back to each one his wage according to his deeds. And after a long time the Lord will give back to each one his wage." "And will there be no mercy for those who are afflicted, lord?" I said. "There will be," he said.

**68:4** "But those who are afflicted and endure their afflictions and are not overcome by them — those who are not broken in mind — these shall receive very great glory from the Lord. Those who are in affliction and do not overcome — those who are broken — shall receive none of this glory, nor shall they live. The one who keeps the commandments and endures through the affliction receives life and grows great in it."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the theology of testing and reward in Similitude 6.*
